USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Why obstruction progresses

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A child with bacterial tracheitis requires airway intervention despite supplemental oxygen and antibiotics. Endoscopy reveals thick adherent material partially occluding the tracheal lumen. Which process most directly explains the persistent mechanical obstruction?

  1. Purulent exudate and sloughed mucosa obstructing the airway
  2. Bronchial smooth-muscle contraction without luminal debris
  3. Extrinsic compression by an enlarged thyroid
  4. Supraglottic edema confined to the epiglottis
  5. Loss of elastic recoil in the distal alveoli
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Purulent exudate and sloughed mucosa obstructing the airway

Infected secretions and mucosal debris can physically narrow or plug the trachea.

Understanding the options

Purulent exudate and sloughed mucosa obstructing the airway
Infected secretions and mucosal debris can physically narrow or plug the trachea.
Bronchial smooth-muscle contraction without luminal debris
Bronchospasm is not the endoscopically observed cause of obstruction in the trachea.
Extrinsic compression by an enlarged thyroid
An external mass would not explain the adherent intraluminal material in an acutely infected trachea.
Supraglottic edema confined to the epiglottis
The obstructing material is visualized in the tracheal lumen rather than confined above the glottis.
Loss of elastic recoil in the distal alveoli
Alveolar recoil abnormalities do not explain this central airway obstruction.
